tests.name: collections
tests.description: The collection operators | (union), in and contains (membership), the Combining functions union(other) and combine(other[, preserveOrder]), and the Subsetting functions single(), first(), last(), tail(), skip(num), take(num), intersect(other), exclude(other). Order is only asserted where the text guarantees it (paths of an instance, exclude(), combine with preserveOrder true, and the positional functions on an ordered input); results of |, union(), intersect() and combine() without preserveOrder are compared by count and supersetOf. Leaves out what the text does not settle: an empty left and right operand of in/contains together, a multi-item left operand of in with an empty right operand, a multi-item right operand of contains, the equality intersect() and exclude() use, which of two equal items union() keeps, an empty num for skip()/take(), an empty or non-Boolean preserveOrder, items of different types compared by in/contains, and whether tail(), skip() and take() must return a result on an input whose order is undefined (the results of | and of combine() without preserveOrder), which the text lets an implementation refuse with an error; for that reason the 3.0.0 worked examples (0 | 1 | 2).tail(), .skip(n) and .take(n) have no case. A num for skip()/take() that is not an Integer and cannot be converted to one ends with an error. The indexer [ ] is not covered.
